title: Cross-team error budget pool and initiative gating playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: As Redwood scales Dedicated and Private customers, multiple platform teams operate services that share common downstream dependencies (serving runtime, KV cache, auth). Siloed error budgets lead to noisy escalation and misprioritization during incidents. We propose a cross-team error budget pooling approach with deterministic gating rules for initiative rollouts to preserve platform SLOs while enabling safe experimentation.

Goals: 1) Define a lightweight pooled error budget model for related services so teams can trade off small short-term SLI regressions against coordinated mitigation. 2) Create a gating playbook for product/engineering initiatives (canary/A-B/feature flags) that enforces hard gates when pooled budgets exceed thresholds. 3) Provide a small set of dashboards and automated alerts showing pool burn, per-team contributions, and rollback recommendations. 4) Ensure the playbook is compatible with Dedicated and Private deployment constraints and can be enforced by Console rollout controls.

Proposal summary: - Pool composition: group services by dependency domain (runtime-core, cache-layer, auth). Each pool has a defined SLI baseline (p99 latency, availability) and an allocated pool error budget derived from historical SLI variance and business priority. - Burn accounting: attribute SLI violations to initiatives via deployment tags and request traces (route/model labels). Use weighted attribution: direct degradations get higher weight than background noise. - Gating thresholds: soft threshold (50% pool burn) triggers advisory notifications and staged rollout throttles; hard threshold (80% pool burn or >5% absolute SLO delta) blocks new canaries and triggers coordinated rollback playbook. - Staggered experiment windows: allow teams to schedule experiment windows to avoid over-concentration; Console will expose a queue and time-based reservations. - Exceptions & overrides: product manager can apply a documented temporary waiver with required mitigation commitments and an explicit rollback time. Waivers are audit-logged.

Telemetry & dashboards: - Pool-level heatmap with 30d and 90d burn trends, per-team contribution bars, and active experiments list. - Per-initiative trace view linking rollout ID -> PR -> metric change. - Alerts: pool-warning@reliability when soft threshold crossed; pool-critical@oncall when hard threshold crossed.

Rollout plan & milestones: - Week 1 (discovery): finalize pool boundaries and SLI baselines with Reliability and Infra teams. - Week 2 (implementation): add rollout tagging in Console + minimal attribution pipeline in telemetry. - Week 3 (pilot): run with two non-customer-impacting initiatives across runtime-core pool. - Week 4 (refine + docs): finalize playbook, create PRD and onboarding checklist for teams. - Week 6 (GA): enable soft enforcement for all teams; GA gating enforcement scheduled in rollout-2026.05.

Acceptance criteria: - Definition doc approved by Reliability, Infra, and PM leads. - Console exposes rollout tagging and experiment reservation UI. - Dashboards show pool burn with attribution and two pilot initiatives complete with postmortems. - Automated alerts trigger at defined thresholds and trigger the rollback runbook link.

Risks & mitigations: - Incorrect attribution causing unfair throttles: mitigate with weighted attribution and manual review window before hard blocks. - Overly conservative gating slows product velocity: pilot and tune thresholds; allow waiver path with audit. - Private deployments without telemetry: require minimum local telemetry shim or make policy advisory for Private customers initially.

Artifacts & links: - PRD (drive): https://drive.google.com/example/prd-cross-team-error-pool - Console ticket for rollout tagging: GH-rlw/console#428 - Telemetry prototype dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.example/d/errpool/pool-heatmap - Pilot retrospective doc: https://docs.redwood.example/pilot-retrospective-error-pool

Next steps: 1) Review pool boundary proposal with Stack Owners (target 2026-03-18) 2) Assign Eng owners for attribution pipeline and Console UI work 3) Draft playbook one-pager and onboarding checklist for PMs and Eng leads.
